name: Sale, VAT 15 %
description: A taxable supply made in Dominica by a taxable person, standard-rated
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, 2005, s. 9(1)(a) — a tax of 15 per cent of the value of every taxable supply by a taxable person in Dominica, accounted for by the person making the supply (s. 9(2)(a)). The Division's VAT page gives the same rate. The base posts to box 1 net of the tax, the tax to box 6 (box numbers are this pack's, see tax_report.json). valid_from is 1 March 2006, the date the tax came into force (Division's VAT page).

name: Retail sale, VAT 15 %, the price includes the tax
description: A standard-rated sale whose price already holds the VAT
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, 2005, s. 9(1)(a) — a tax of 15 per cent of the value of every taxable supply by a taxable person in Dominica, accounted for by the person making the supply (s. 9(2)(a)). The Division's VAT page gives the same rate. The Act's tax fraction (s. 2, R/(100+R)) extracts the tax from a price that includes it, which is what price_include does: 115.00 holds 100.00 and 15.00. Same boxes as DM-S-15.

name: Sale of accommodation or dive activity, VAT 10 %
description: Accommodation by a hotel, guest house, inn or similar establishment, or the dive activity portion of a dive package
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, 2005, s. 9(1)(c) and (d) (the latter added by the Value Added Tax (Amendment) Act, 2006) — 10 per cent, to the extent provided in regulations; Regulations reg. 5 applies it to accommodation by a hotel, guest house, inn or similar establishment and to a furnished apartment or room, not to a renter in a private home. The Division's VAT page names accommodation and diving activity. The pack does not decide which of a user's supplies qualify: that is the user's, with their accountant. Base to box 2, tax to box 7.

name: Zero-rated supply (export)
description: An export of goods or services, zero-rated
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, 2005, s. 17 and Schedule I, paragraph 3 — exported goods and services are charged at zero per cent; Schedule I, paragraph 3(1)(a) requires the goods to have been entered for export and exported by the supplier. A zero-rated supply is a taxable supply: the input tax of what produces it stays deductible. Base to box 3.

name: Zero-rated supply in Dominica
description: A domestic supply of Schedule I at zero per cent (for instance basic foods, certain medical devices and agricultural and fishing inputs)
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, 2005, s. 17 and Schedule I — the Division's registration guide lists the zero-rated supplies, among them exported goods and services, certain agricultural inputs, certain medical devices and supplies, basic foods (rice, sugar, milk and flour) and certain fishing inputs. The pack does not reproduce the schedule: the user checks the item against it. Base to box 3.

name: Exempt supply
description: A supply of Schedule II (for instance financial services, residential rent, education), outside the tax
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, 2005, s. 18 and Schedule II — exempt supplies are not subject to the tax and the input tax of what is acquired to make them is not deductible; the Division's registration guide lists financial services, the sale of real property, residential rents, water supplied by DOWASCO, veterinary and education services, unprocessed agricultural products sold by the producer and the transport of goods and passengers by land. Base to box 4.

name: Purchase, VAT 15 %
description: A purchase from a taxable person, standard-rated, with a tax invoice
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, 2005, s. 25(1)(a) — the input tax payable on taxable supplies made to the person for use in a taxable activity is deductible, on a tax invoice or a tax debit or credit note (s. 25(2)). Base to box 10, tax to box 12. Section 26 (apportionment for mixed supplies and the disallowed categories) is the user's.

name: Purchase of accommodation or dive activity, VAT 10 %
description: Accommodation or dive activity bought for the business at the reduced rate
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, 2005, s. 9(1)(c), (d) and s. 25(1)(a) — input tax at the 10 per cent rate is deductible on the same conditions as at 15 per cent. Base to box 10, tax to box 12.

name: Import of goods, VAT 15 %
description: Goods imported: the VAT paid to the Comptroller of Customs
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, 2005, s. 9(1)(b), s. 20 and s. 22 — 15 per cent of the value of an import of goods, paid by the importer on the import declaration (s. 9(2)(b)); the value for tax is the customs value plus freight and insurance, duty and the customs service charge (s. 20(1)), which the pack does not compute: it applies 15 % to the invoice value and the customs entry is the user's. The tax paid is deductible (s. 25(1)(a)). Base to box 9, tax to box 11.

name: Purchase without VAT
description: A purchase of a zero-rated or exempt supply, or from a person who charges no VAT: no input tax to claim
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, 2005, s. 17 and s. 18 — a zero-rated supply carries tax at zero per cent and an exempt supply carries none, so the purchaser has no input tax to claim; the value is still reported among the purchases of the period (box 10).
